criticalCorrections: Huygens 1675 concerns the balance spring, not invention of the complete modern Swiss lever escapement. The Met's contemporary watch retains a verge escapement.

The approximate thirty-part reduction concerns a regulating assembly. GPHG prose also uses 31 and AWCI counts twelve under another boundary. No universal exact thirty-part bill is asserted. Intermediate slider counts are transition indicators only.
The separate silicon escape wheel remains. Winding, barrel, transmission and hand indication are not replaced by the oscillator plate.

A monocrystalline silicon plate is patterned by micromachining. The patent lists DRIE among possible methods. It is not cast. Thickness 0.5 mm and compliant blade in-plane width about 20 micrometres are different dimensions.

The centre is fixed at three mounting points. Outer regions oscillate through a small angle, flexing compliant connections. They are not stationary while only the inner arms move, and they do not make continuous revolutions.
15 Hz means fifteen full oscillations and thirty half-oscillations per second, giving 108000 vibrations per hour. Six degrees each way is a separate amplitude quantity.

The 2017 award release's mean 0.3 s/day and precision over 95 percent of reserve are attributed manufacturer claims. Isochronism concerns period dependence on amplitude, not necessarily constant amplitude.

Lab reserve conflicts between GPHG's 60-hour heading and 55-hour prose. The article explicitly uses the original 2017 award release's 60 hours. Inventor reserve and water resistance conflict between GPHG and FHH and are omitted.
The 1100-gauss figure is a stated completed-watch test level, not absolute magnetic immunity under every exposure. A higher frequency alone does not guarantee a daily rate.

The regulating organ removes several lubricated pivot interfaces. The complete watch is not frictionless, lubricant-free, lossless or immune to all wear. Elasticity does not eliminate internal damping or contact interactions.
Lab 2017 ZO 342 operates at 15 Hz. Inventor 2019 Calibre 9100 operates at 18 Hz. Later Inventor innovations are not backdated to Lab.
A visually smooth seconds hand still advances through discrete escapement-mediated increments. No light emission or mathematically continuous transmission is claimed.

finiteElements.type: Assembled linear Euler–Bernoulli beam element matrix, two degrees of freedom per node, cubic Hermite interpolation, dense Gaussian elimination with pivoting
finiteElements.boundaryConditions: Left displacement and rotation fixed. Right end has prescribed lateral displacement and zero rotation. No axial force or distributed load.
finiteElements.materialQualification: Isotropic scalar teaching approximation, not Zenith wafer orientation or an anisotropic plate tensor. Real monocrystalline silicon depends on direction.
finiteElements.outputs: Displacement, curvature, surface normal bending stress, end reaction and strain energy 0.5*d^T*K*d. Colour shows absolute surface stress, not von Mises stress.
finiteElements.colourScale: Fixed over each selected load amplitude, not renormalized to each animation frame. It reaches blue at zero curvature/loading rather than always showing red.
finiteElements.validation: For this imposed-end-displacement case the analytical solution is cubic and is reproduced by the beam interpolation for all tested meshes. Doubling displacement doubles stress and quadruples energy. Both end signs reverse and centre bending stress vanishes.
finiteElements.limits: Separate beam bench, not a finite-element analysis of the full Zenith plate. Displayed deformation is amplified. No eigenmode, contact dynamics, molecular/atomic simulation, fracture prediction or rate certification. No claim of 1000 rendered frames per second.

workshop.handComparison: 4 Hz and 15 Hz with one illustrative hand increment per half-oscillation, 8 versus 30 steps per second. Both average one turn per minute. The hand clock is real-time while the oscillator is slowed. This is not a measured reproduction of a production transmission.
workshop.visualQualifications: Silicon is not transparent sapphire. Blue indicates the moving plate. The wire grid shows continuum deformation, not atoms. No fake radiated light or optical trail.
